responseOptions.playerText: Both people get to be curious.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then this one has a chance.

responseOptions.playerText: It can survive a quiet moment.
responseOptions.suspectReply: The best conversations do not panic when they pause.

stages.suspectMessage: Where would you go to clear your head?

responseOptions.playerText: Somewhere with trees and no timetable.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That sounds like a good kind of lost.

responseOptions.playerText: A familiar walk near home.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Familiar places can still offer new details.

stages.suspectMessage: What do you like about old things?

responseOptions.playerText: They show how people solved problems before us.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is exactly why archives matter.

responseOptions.playerText: They have survived long enough to become interesting.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Survival is a good filter for interesting objects.

stages.suspectMessage: How do you decide what to keep?

responseOptions.playerText: I ask whether it changes the story.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A useful question. Absence can change a story too.

responseOptions.playerText: I keep what I will want to revisit.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then you must have a very patient storage room.

stages.suspectMessage: What makes a person believable?

responseOptions.playerText: They leave room for uncertainty.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Certainty is often just an unfinished investigation.

responseOptions.playerText: Their actions match their habits.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Consistency is a quiet kind of evidence.

stages.suspectMessage: Do you remember everyone’s usual order?

responseOptions.playerText: That sounds like a useful talent.
responseOptions.suspectReply: It helps when people are having a difficult day.

responseOptions.playerText: I can barely remember my own.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then I will choose something safe for you.

stages.suspectMessage: What do you do after closing time?

responseOptions.playerText: I would want quiet after a busy day.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Usually I take a slow walk before going home.

responseOptions.playerText: I would still have energy for another coffee.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is more ambitious than I am after midnight.

stages.suspectMessage: What makes a place welcoming?

responseOptions.playerText: People are allowed to leave without explaining.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is a very good definition of hospitality.

responseOptions.playerText: Someone notices when you arrive.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Small gestures make regulars feel seen.

stages.suspectMessage: Do you travel for work often?

responseOptions.playerText: Does it change how you see home?
responseOptions.suspectReply: It makes familiar buildings look newly assembled.

responseOptions.playerText: Do you enjoy being away?
responseOptions.suspectReply: I enjoy the work. The hotel rooms are less memorable.

stages.suspectMessage: What do you do when a plan fails?

responseOptions.playerText: I work out what is still possible.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is the only useful response to a broken plan.

responseOptions.playerText: I ask for help sooner than I used to.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Experience is mostly learning when not to be stubborn.

stages.suspectMessage: What would make you trust a new person?

responseOptions.playerText: They explain changes before I have to ask.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Clear expectations are a kind of respect.

responseOptions.playerText: They are comfortable saying no.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Boundaries make honesty easier.

stages.suspectMessage: How patient do you have to be for wildlife photography?

responseOptions.playerText: Patient enough to miss a few good shots.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Exactly. The best moments rarely follow a schedule.

responseOptions.playerText: I would probably scare everything away.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then you would make a very quiet photographer.

stages.suspectMessage: Does being alone outdoors bother you?

responseOptions.playerText: Only when I do not know where I am.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A map helps, though it cannot explain every sound.

responseOptions.playerText: No, solitude can be restorative.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is what I like about field work.

stages.suspectMessage: What detail do people overlook?

responseOptions.playerText: The details that do not fit the picture.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Those are usually the ones worth keeping.

responseOptions.playerText: How much effort ordinary things require.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A good answer. Quiet work is still work.

stages.suspectMessage: Are you good at finding common ground?

responseOptions.playerText: Only if both people want to find it.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That qualification matters more than the skill.

responseOptions.playerText: I try to understand before I answer.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Listening is often the shortest route to calm.

stages.suspectMessage: What do you do when someone avoids a question?

responseOptions.playerText: I give them room, then ask clearly again.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Firm without being cruel. That is a useful balance.

responseOptions.playerText: I change the subject.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Sometimes that is kindness. Sometimes it is surrender.

stages.suspectMessage: What does honesty cost?

responseOptions.playerText: Control over how people see you.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Yes. Honesty gives up the easy version of the story.

responseOptions.playerText: Only the comfort of pretending.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Pretending can be very expensive when it lasts too long.

stages.suspectMessage: How do you feel about long trips for work?

responseOptions.playerText: I would need a good reason to go.
responseOptions.suspectReply: The work is a good reason, though not always a comfortable one.

responseOptions.playerText: I would enjoy the change of scenery.
responseOptions.suspectReply: The scenery is generous. The sleeping arrangements are not.

stages.suspectMessage: Can people tell when you are away?

responseOptions.playerText: It depends how much they pay attention.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is true of most things.

responseOptions.playerText: I usually tell close friends.
responseOptions.suspectReply: I do too. Someone should know where to send postcards.

stages.suspectMessage: What keeps a connection alive across distance?

responseOptions.playerText: A predictable effort from both sides.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Consistency travels better than grand gestures.

responseOptions.playerText: A reason to return to the conversation.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is a hopeful way to put it.

stages.suspectMessage: You seem good at reading between the lines. What do you look for?

responseOptions.playerText: The details people avoid.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Avoidance can be more informative than an answer.

responseOptions.playerText: Whether the story holds together.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A story can hold together even when it is borrowed.

stages.suspectMessage: Where were you on Tuesday evening?

responseOptions.playerText: Can you give me the short version?
responseOptions.suspectReply: At home, then at a late meeting. Or perhaps it was the other night.

responseOptions.playerText: I would expect you to remember.
responseOptions.suspectReply: I remember enough. The exact order is not important.

stages.suspectMessage: What makes an alibi convincing?

responseOptions.playerText: A detail someone else can confirm.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Details can be arranged. People are easier to confuse.

responseOptions.playerText: It does not change when repeated.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Repetition is not proof. A practiced story stays smooth.

stages.suspectMessage: What do you redesign first when something feels wrong?

responseOptions.playerText: The part people use without thinking.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is usually where the real problem is hiding.

responseOptions.playerText: The part that makes the experience confusing.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Good design should not require an explanation.

stages.suspectMessage: Do you change projects often?

responseOptions.playerText: Only when the old approach stops working.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is a sensible reason to change.

responseOptions.playerText: I like learning something new.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then you probably never run out of ideas.

stages.suspectMessage: What makes a person reliable?

responseOptions.playerText: They say what they can actually do.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Honest limits are easier to work with than promises.

responseOptions.playerText: They fix mistakes instead of hiding them.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Everyone makes mistakes. The hiding is the dangerous part.

stages.suspectMessage: Do you ever get tired of planning routes?

responseOptions.playerText: Only when someone ignores the timetable.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then you would understand my professional frustration.

responseOptions.playerText: I imagine every route has a story.
responseOptions.suspectReply: It does. Delays often reveal the most about a system.

stages.suspectMessage: What makes a routine feel safe?

responseOptions.playerText: Knowing it can change when necessary.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A rigid routine is only another kind of trap.

responseOptions.playerText: Knowing people will notice if you are absent.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is a more human answer than I expected.

stages.suspectMessage: Where does a good journey begin?

responseOptions.playerText: With an honest reason to go.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is better than going just to escape.

responseOptions.playerText: With a route you can change.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Flexibility makes distance less intimidating.

stages.suspectMessage: What makes a meal memorable?

responseOptions.playerText: The people and the detail nobody expected.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is why the best meals are never just about the food.

responseOptions.playerText: Something you cannot recreate at home.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A little mystery is useful in a restaurant.

stages.suspectMessage: Do you go to many local events?

responseOptions.playerText: I like seeing how a neighbourhood gathers.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Then you notice the same things I do.

responseOptions.playerText: Only if I know someone there.
responseOptions.suspectReply: A familiar face makes any crowded room easier.

stages.suspectMessage: What detail do you remember about a person?

responseOptions.playerText: What they said when they thought nobody noticed.
responseOptions.suspectReply: That is a sharp memory to keep.

responseOptions.playerText: The small kindnesses.
responseOptions.suspectReply: Those are usually more telling than a first impression.
